title: openai-v1-chat: stream buffering resilience + role normalizer and logprob passthrough
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Add stream buffering resilience with KV prefetch, normalize OpenAI v1 chat role aliases, and introduce logprob_passthrough param for parity. No user-facing breaking changes.
description:
Summary: This PR implements three coordinated pieces to improve OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity and streaming stability: 1) a stream buffering layer that reduces partial-fragment dropouts and stabilizes function_call/tool-call handoffs under high concurrency, 2) a role normalizer that canonicalizes role aliases (assistant/ai/bot -> assistant; human/user/client -> user) and enforces role hygiene when migrating from legacy param shapes, and 3) a logprob_passthrough toggle that preserves token-level logprobs coming from model backends and surfaces them through the OpenAI-compatible envelope when enabled.

Motivation: Customers reported intermittent missing logprobs in streamed fragments and tool-call framing jitter when the KV cache prefetch overlapped with first-token emission. At the same time, a few customers rely on loose role naming ("bot", "human") which resulted in inconsistent behavior during assistant routing and stop token application.

Goals: - Eliminate stream fragment dropouts and reduce observed rebuffer events by >90% in canary workloads - Provide a safe, opt-in way to preserve provider-native logprob outputs for downstream evals - Make OpenAI role aliases transparent and backward compatible

Changes made (high level): - runtime/streaming/stream_buffer.rs: Introduces StreamBuffer with a windowed queue and backpressure-aware flush. Adds per-request prefetch fence for KV cache so first-token emission waits for a minimal prefetch if configured. - api/openai_adapter/v1_chat_adapter.py: Adds role normalizer function; maps legacy role names into canonical roles and emits warning telemetry when aliases are used. Adds new parameter mapping for 'logprob_passthrough' -> internal flag. - handlers/stream_coordinator.go: Integrates buffer handshake into function_call/tool-call path to ensure tool payloads are framed atomically with stream fragments. - tests/e2e/openai_streaming_stability_test.go: New end-to-end test that replays production fragment sequences with injected prefetch delays. - docs/openai_v1_migration.md: Documented role aliasing and the new logprob_passthrough flag, including examples and caveats.

Commits (summary): - Add StreamBuffer and KV prefetch fence (5 commits) - Wire OpenAI adapter to normalized roles and params (3 commits) - Stabilize tool-call framing and add end-to-end tests (2 commits) - Docs and release notes (1 commit)

Files changed (high level): - runtime/streaming/stream_buffer.rs - api/openai_adapter/v1_chat_adapter.py - handlers/stream_coordinator.go - models/role_normalizer.py - tests/e2e/openai_streaming_stability_test.go - docs/openai_v1_migration.md - several small refs and test fixtures

Review conversation (condensed): - Priya: "Can the prefetch fence be toggled per-deployment? We need to avoid global latency regressions." Author: "Yes, added a per-request hint and a global knob. Default is off for latency-sensitive customers; enabled for canaries and regressions." - Liam: "I saw a flake in CI for the tool-call framing test under race conditions." Author: "Fixed via a tighter handshake and added a deterministic scheduler in the test harness; re-ran CI." - Marisol: "Are we confident about telemetry volume from role alias warnings?" Author: "We consolidated alias warnings to sampled telemetry (1%) and emit a single aggregated counter per request batch to avoid noise."

CI summary: - unit (linux): pass - integration (k8s): pass - e2e canary replay: pass - lint/format: pass - security scan: pass

Performance and safety notes: - Canary on dedicated pool showed 0.8% median latency impact when KV prefetch is enabled, but 92% reduction in observed stream rebuffer events for the tested workloads. - Default behavior (no KV prefetch) preserves current latency profile; the prefetch fence is opt-in via API param or deployment config. - The role normalizer is backward-compatible and only rewrites role values before routing; the original role string is still available in metadata for auditing. - logprob_passthrough defaults to false; enabling it may increase payload sizes.

Migration notes: - Customers using non-standard role names do not need to change code; the adapter normalizes names automatically. We recommend explicitly using canonical roles going forward to avoid subtle stop-token mismatches in downstream tooling. - If you rely on per-token logprobs for evals, flip logprob_passthrough=true in your request to get provider-native logprobs; this flag is currently gated for enterprise plans and may require coordination.

Merge outcome: Squash and merge to main. Merged by Priya Kumar after all approvals and green CI. Backports: Cherrypick to release/2026-02 (patch) queued.

Tickets / follow-ups: - ENG-2203: Add metrics for "stream_buffer.backpressure_time" to Console dashboard - ENG-2204: Add configuration UI in Dedicated admin console for prefetch knob - ENG-2210: Run broader canary across multiple regions for edge cases
commits_summary: Add stream buffering primitives; KV prefetch fence; role normalizer; logprob passthrough param; tool-call framing fixes; e2e tests and docs (total 11 commits).
notes_on_testing: Added deterministic scheduler for race reproduction; e2e replay test reproduces prior flaky trace and verifies no dropout under prefetch handshake; load tested at 200 RPS per worker for 30 minutes in canary pool.
